symbols.name: digit width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in one radix digit.
symbols.quote: Let $k$ be the number of bits in one radix digit, so the digit base is $2^k$, and let $m$ be the number of digits in each integer.

symbols.name: digits per integer
symbols.meaning: The number of digits in each integer.
symbols.quote: Let $k$ be the number of bits in one radix digit, so the digit base is $2^k$, and let $m$ be the number of digits in each integer.

symbols.name: first integer
symbols.meaning: The first of the two integers to be multiplied, below $2^{km}$.
symbols.quote: Take integers $u$ and $v$ below $2^{km}$, whose $i$-th digits are $u_i$ and $v_i$, each in $\{0,\dots,2^k-1\}$.

symbols.name: second integer
symbols.meaning: The second of the two integers to be multiplied, below $2^{km}$.
symbols.quote: Take integers $u$ and $v$ below $2^{km}$, whose $i$-th digits are $u_i$ and $v_i$, each in $\{0,\dots,2^k-1\}$.

symbols.name: digit of u
symbols.quote: Take integers $u$ and $v$ below $2^{km}$, whose $i$-th digits are $u_i$ and $v_i$, each in $\{0,\dots,2^k-1\}$.

symbols.name: digit of v
symbols.quote: Take integers $u$ and $v$ below $2^{km}$, whose $i$-th digits are $u_i$ and $v_i$, each in $\{0,\dots,2^k-1\}$.

symbols.name: indeterminate
symbols.meaning: The variable of the digit polynomials, an indeterminate.
symbols.quote: Let $z$ be an indeterminate and let $U(z)=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1} u_i z^i$ and $V(z)=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1} v_i z^i$ be the polynomials whose coefficient lists are the digits of $u$ and $v$, so that $u=U(2^k)$ and $v=V(2^k)$.

symbols.name: digit polynomial of u
symbols.meaning: The polynomial whose coefficient list is the digits of $u$.
symbols.quote: Let $z$ be an indeterminate and let $U(z)=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1} u_i z^i$ and $V(z)=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1} v_i z^i$ be the polynomials whose coefficient lists are the digits of $u$ and $v$, so that $u=U(2^k)$ and $v=V(2^k)$.

symbols.name: digit polynomial of v
symbols.meaning: The polynomial whose coefficient list is the digits of $v$.
symbols.quote: Let $z$ be an indeterminate and let $U(z)=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1} u_i z^i$ and $V(z)=\sum_{i=0}^{m-1} v_i z^i$ be the polynomials whose coefficient lists are the digits of $u$ and $v$, so that $u=U(2^k)$ and $v=V(2^k)$.

symbols.name: product polynomial
symbols.quote: Let $W=UV$ be their product, whose coefficient of $z^j$ is $w_j=\sum_{i+l=j} u_i v_l$; this convolution of the digit lists gives $uv=W(2^k)$.

symbols.name: convolution coefficient
symbols.meaning: The coefficient of $z^j$ in $W$, a sum of products of digits.
symbols.quote: Let $W=UV$ be their product, whose coefficient of $z^j$ is $w_j=\sum_{i+l=j} u_i v_l$; this convolution of the digit lists gives $uv=W(2^k)$.

relations.quote: Splitting integers into radix digits reduces [Exact integer multiplication](exact-integer-multiplication.md) to convolution of short integer coefficients.
